transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Leah O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Anika Bose (LyricSoft Head of ML), Tom Whittaker (Platform Engineer), Priya Rao (CTO), Jared Kim (SRE)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on workload shape, success criteria, benchmarks and timeline. Focus: QPS/concurrency targets, input/output token distributions, tail latency targets, and what data replay artifacts LyricSoft can provide. Agreed to run traffic replay using Redwood replay kit; SE to map baseline capacity and propose dedicated vs hosted tradeoff.

Topics covered:
- Current production traffic shape and variability
- Typical prompt/input sizes and output token distributions
- Target QPS and concurrency for POC (steady-state + burst)
- Success criteria: latency p95/p99, error rates, cost per 1k tokens
- Benchmark plan & timeline
- Security and data residency questions

Action items (recap):
- Maya: send benchmark template + instructions (replay tool)
- Tom: provide 48 hours of anonymized traffic (CSV) + sample prompts
- Carlos: prepare capacity mapping and SLA proposals for two scenarios (hosted + dedicated)
- Leah: include SOC2 docs and encryption/KMS notes

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick introductions? We have Maya and Carlos from Redwood, Leah here too.
[00:06] Anika: Hi, yes Anika from LyricSoft. We're excited — been looking at Redwood for inference cost and tail latency stuff.
[00:11] Tom: Tom here. I'll be owner for the traffic artifacts.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, CTO. I'll be on high-level success criteria. Jared's on for SRE questions.
[00:20] Maya: Great. The goal today is to scope a POC to run a traffic replay and measure tail latency and throughput, and to define success criteria. Can you tell us current QPS and typical concurrency?
[00:32] Anika: Sure. Peak user facing QPS is around 220 QPS during business hours, but the back of our pipeline hits spiky bursts up to 900 QPS for short periods, like 10 to 30 seconds. Average is more like 45 QPS. Concurrency per model instance is a hard number because we multiplex requests across microservices.
[00:50] Carlos: When you say "spiky bursts", are those sustained or short microbursts? 900 for 10 to 30 seconds suggests very bursty. That matters for auto-scale.
[00:58] Anika: Right, short microbursts. Also we have heavy tail tokens when users ask for summaries — output tokens can be 800 to 1,200 but median is 210. Input prompts are usually 60 to 120 tokens.
[01:12] Maya: Ok interesting. So token distribution is skewed — lots of short responses and a few very long responses. For the POC we usually ask for a 48 hour traffic sample, anonymized, with timestamps and token counts per request. That lets us build a QPS surface and a burst profile.
[01:28] Tom: We can do that. We'll need the exact CSV schema.
[01:31] Maya: I'll send the template after the call. It includes epoch ms timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, model_hint, and a sample prompt id.
[01:40] Jared: Quick security note — we need to be clear on what data leaves our VPC. LyricSoft prefers Private deployment for PII-sensitive prompts.
[01:50] Leah: We can run the replay from your VPC using a private deployment connector. But for initial benchmarking hosted mode is faster to iterate. There is a tradeoff.
[01:59] Priya: What's the difference in expected tail latency between hosted and dedicated? Some rough ballpark.
[02:04] Carlos: Ballpark: for a 256 token average response, hosted can be ~120–220ms p95 depending on model, whereas dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized batching can shave off 20–40% on throughput-sensitive workloads. But p99 tails depend a lot on burst handling and KV cache warmness.
[02:22] Anika: Our initial success bar is p95 < 300ms for 256-token outputs and p99 < 600ms for typical mixed workloads. Does that sound achievable?
[02:31] Carlos: It's reasonable as a target for the POC, we'll validate on the replay. We should also set an error budget for rejects/timeouts — e.g., <0.2% errors.
[02:39] Tom: Cost is another axis — can you estimate cost per 1k tokens for dedicated vs hosted?
[02:44] Maya: We'll share rough pricing tiers but a baseline POC cost estimate will depend on peak concurrency and how many hours you're running the replay. The replay usually runs at scaled QPS to simulate peaks for short windows.
[02:55] Anika: For the replay, we want two scenarios: steady-state day load (45 QPS) and burst scenario (simulate 900 QPS for 30s bursts repeated every 10 minutes).
[03:07] Carlos: Good. We'll design the benchmark harness to replay both patterns. We'll also instrument token-level latency so we can see where the tail tokens are coming from.
[03:16] Priya: On security: we need SSO, SAML, RBAC, and KMS integration. Any issues with bringing your control plane into our VPC?
[03:26] Leah: We have a Private deployment option that uses customer-managed control plane and supports KMS/HSM integrations and SSO. We'll send the architecture doc.
[03:33] Maya: For the POC success criteria let's record what we heard: p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens, p99 < 600ms for mixed, error rate < 0.2%, and cost below a threshold TBD. Anything to add?
[03:45] Priya: Add that model fidelity must match current outputs — no regressions on answer quality. We'll supply a small test set for quality baseline.
[03:51] Carlos: We'll run differential quality checks using your sample prompts. If we see regressions we'll flag them and iterate on quantization/config.
[03:58] Anika: About model variants — we currently use an open LLM stack. We might want to test a larger model for a subset of requests (long summaries) and a smaller fast model for chat. Can Redwood route by policy?
[04:09] Maya: Yes, smart routing is part of our platform. For the POC we can simulate routing by marking model_hint in the CSV so the replay uses different model families for different request classes.
[04:20] Tom: On telemetry, what traces/metrics do you provide during the replay? We want per-request token latency, queue depth, and host-level GPU utilization.
[04:28] Carlos: We surface token-level latency, batching stats, queue depth, GPU util, and KV cache hit rates. We'll give you a dashboard link for post-run analysis.
[04:36] Anika: Great. Any gotchas you've seen with traffic replays?
[04:40] Carlos: A few: timestamp skew, truncated prompts during anonymization, and missing model hints. Also if the replay is too synthetic it hides network variability; we prefer using real timestamps and simulating clocks.
[04:50] Maya: We'll provide the replay SDK and instructions. Tom, you mentioned S3 — we can accept the CSV in S3 or upload to our secure share.
[04:58] Tom: S3 works. We'll need a short checklist to ensure the data is anonymized.
[05:04] Leah: We'll add the checklist to the template. Also note on encryption: server-side encryption + customer KMS is supported.
[05:11] Priya: Timeline? We want this POC done before end of month if possible. That gives ~2 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:16] Carlos: Two weeks is tight but doable for a basic run: 48 hour data ingestion and one benchmark run plus analysis. For a deeper dedicated scenario we'd need 3–4 weeks to provision and test.
[05:26] Maya: Proposed timeline: today: share template and security pack; by 9/24 customer provides CSV; week of 9/29 we run replay and initial benchmark; week of 10/6 we review detailed results and capacity planning.
[05:38] Anika: Works for us. One more question: for the POC do you allow us to pin model weights/version so we can compare exactly?
[05:46] Carlos: Yes you can pin model versions for reproducibility. We'll also snapshot runtime config used for the test.
[05:52] Tom: Are you able to simulate token caching / KV cache warm starts? Because our production has large prefix reuse.
[05:58] Carlos: We can simulate warm cache by seeding the KV cache or running a warmup phase before the measured run. We'll include that option.
[06:05] Maya: Any contractual stuff we need to flag? Priya?
[06:08] Priya: Nothing heavy for POC but legal will want an NDA and export controls reviewed.
[06:13] Leah: We'll send the standard POC agreement and SOC2 pack.
[06:17] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps...
[06:20] [recap] Maya: I'll send replay template, checklist, SOC2 docs; Carlos will draft capacity mapping; Tom will upload anonymized traffic; schedule run week of 9/29.
[06:30] Anika: Thanks all. Looking forward to the replay.
[06:33] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared thread.

End of transcript.

Notes on artifacts to share: replay SDK link (will be in email), benchmark template CSV, SOC2 + security pack, initial rough pricing tiers, sample dashboard from previous similar POC (anonymized).
